title: Command and Control Interface Control Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
6. MOS 7216, Command and Control Interface Control Officer (III) (CWO5 to
WO) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Command and Control Interface Control Officers (C2ICO)
analyze, plan, design, execute, and manage the marine corps functional
component’s common tactical pictures (CTP) and integrate the service’s CTP
with the joint task force (JTF) commander’s common operational picture (COP).
As a member of the operations section (S-3, G-3), the C2ICO is the senior ICO
in support of USMC multi-tactical data link network (MTN) operations and is
the USMC MTN coordinator for the joint data network within a theater/joint
operations area. The C2ICO ensures available interfaces are optimized to
achieve the end-to-end information exchange requirements and flow required to
execute advanced digital mission threads and kill chains in a naval and joint
force environment. This is a highly technical MOS and requires that the
C2ICO be educated and thoroughly knowledgeable in tactical data link (TDL)
theory, multi-TDL architecture planning and design, link 16 network design,
COP/TDL systems and capabilities, advanced TDL techniques, differing TDL
systems and applications, and air defense, air surveillance, and TDL
capabilities of US, coalition, and allied partners. Operating forces billet
assignments for this officer includes marine forces command, marine forces
pacific, marine forces Europe/Africa, marine expeditionary force, marine
division, marine air wing, marine air control group, and marine littoral
regiment. Non-operating forces billet assignments for the C2ICO includes
instructor billet at the Joint Interoperability and Data Link Training Center
(JID-TC), Requirements officer at Marine Corps Combat Development Command,
TDL acquisition project officer at Marine Corps Systems Command, Integration
Officer under Deputy Commandant for Aviation, TDL Instructor at Marine
Aviation Weapons and Tactics Squadron, and project officer at Marine Corps



                                           1-265                        Enclosure (1)
 1141                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



Tactical Systems Support Activity. C2ICOs will often work with joint,
coalition, and other allied TDL partners to provide marine corps TDL
expertise.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOSs 7212, 7236, 7242, 7257, or 7291.

            (2) Must have successfully completed the following JID-TC courses:

                (a) JT-201 Multi-TDL Network Planners Course (A05KHY1).

                (b) JT-102 Multi-TDL Advanced Joint Interoperability Course
(A05L6Z1).

        (3) Security requirement: eligible for top secret with sensitive
compartmented information security clearance.

        (4) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (M02RMN4)
and then the Aviation Command and Control Commons Course (M09C2A1) within 18
months of appointment to WO.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Responsible to unit commanders for composite tracking network
(CTN)/cooperative engagement capability (CEC)/TDL integration, management,
and operations, and ensures all subordinate TDL personnel are adequately
trained to support the command’s mission.

        (2) Provide information concerning capabilities, limitations, and
reliability of CTN and TDL systems and equipment.

        (3) Control and act as the coordinating authority for all subordinate
USMC ICOs, data link coordinators, and unit CEC/TDL managers.

        (4) Responsible for track data coordination across the joint
interface to include resolving ID conflicts, dual designations, and other
interface anomalies.

        (5) Ensures all platform interfaces are configured and operational
according to the published operations task link (OPTASKLINK) and assist the
JICO with developing the OPTASKLINK.

            (6) Coordinate with the JICO/JICC of the assigned area of operations.

        (7) Manage USMC platform-unique composite tracking network and
tactical data link capabilities within the MTN.

        (8) Coordinate with network design facilities to ensure USMC
platforms are accurately designed in link-16 networks.

        (9) Coordinate spectrum requirements with the proper authorities per
operational requirements.




                                        1-266                        Enclosure (1)
 1141                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



        (10) Maintain a thorough familiarity with current and emerging
command and control systems, tactical data links, composite tracking network
equipment, active and passive sensors, and network enabled weapon systems.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Command and Control Center Officers 55-1013.

        (2) Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders, All
Other 55-1019.

            (3) First-Line Supervisors of Weapons Specialists/Crew Members 55-
2012.

            (4) Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Air Battle Manager, 13B.

            (2) Operations Warrant Officer, 7120.

            (3) Command and Control Systems Technician, 140AT2.

d. Duties (1) Responsible to unit commanders for composite tracking network (CTN)/cooperative engagement capability (CEC)/TDL integration, management, and operations, and ensures all subordinate TDL personnel are adequately trained to support the command’s mission.
Evaluate sources of information to determine any limitations, in terms of reliability or usability.
(2) Provide information concerning capabilities, limitations, and reliability of CTN and TDL systems and equipment.
Oversee all communications within specifically assigned territories.
(3) Control and act as the coordinating authority for all subordinate USMC ICOs, data link coordinators, and unit CEC/TDL managers.
Coordinate and link the computer systems within an organization to increase compatibility so that information can be shared.
(4) Responsible for track data coordination across the joint interface to include resolving ID conflicts, dual designations, and other interface anomalies.

Establish functional or system standards to address operational requirements, quality requirements, and design constraints.
(9) Coordinate spectrum requirements with the proper authorities per operational requirements.
Maintain awareness of advances in medicine, computerized diagnostic and treatment equipment, data processing technology, government regulations, health insurance changes, and financing options.

(10) Maintain a thorough familiarity with current and emerging command and control systems, tactical data links, composite tracking network equipment, active and passive sensors, and network enabled weapon systems.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
